workflows.name: ai-slop-remediation
workflows.description: Take an existing site that reads as AI-generated and make it read as designed — detect with evidence, group into root causes, delete before adding, rebuild the three systems, and re-measure until the S1 count is zero without flattening the site's character.
workflows.trigger: An existing website, landing page or application surface that stakeholders describe as "generic", "template-y" or "obviously AI-made"; or a pre-launch review that failed the slop gate in workflows/build-website stage 9.
workflows.not_for: Building a new site from scratch (use workflows/build-website, which prevents the slop rather than removing it); purely internal tooling where utility is the only requirement and the owner has said so; a deliberate brutalist or maximalist design — apply the craft checks but not the restraint checks; an accessibility or performance problem mislabelled as a design problem.
workflows.estimated_duration: hours for a landing page; days for a multi-page product surface

stages.name: Establish the target
stages.goal: Define what "designed" means for this specific product, audience and brand — otherwise remediation replaces one cliché with another.
inputs: 3-6 reference products at the target quality level
outputs: Design Direction Brief with intended impression
stages.exit_gate: A written direction exists with explicit rejections, or the owner has accepted a conventional direction in writing and the remediation scope is limited to craft and consistency.
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate. Remediating without a target produces a different default, not a better design.

stages.name: Capture at full coverage
stages.goal: Collect the evidence base — every template and state, at every required breakpoint, in both themes.
stages.exit_gate: Every template is captured in default, hover, focus, empty, loading, error and modal-open states, at every breakpoint, in both themes.
stages.on_gate_failure: Complete the capture. A review at 1440 px only will miss the majority of real defects.

stages.name: Detect mechanically
stages.goal: Run the full slop catalogue against source and captures, producing symptoms with IDs, evidence and severity.
outputs: evidence at file:line or screenshot reference
stages.exit_gate: Every symptom carries a catalogue ID and concrete evidence, and the source has been grepped for the tell-tale tokens (backdrop-filter, gradient utilities, blur, indigo/purple ramps, pulse/bounce animations, filler adjectives, unsubstantiated metrics).
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove symptoms that have no evidence. An unevidenced symptom is a taste judgement, and it discredits the rest of the report.

stages.name: Measure the systems
stages.goal: Quantify the underlying disorder — spacing values, type sizes, hues, radii, shadows — so the fix targets the cause.
outputs: audit table of distinct values per property
stages.exit_gate: Distinct spacing values, font sizes, saturated hues, radii and shadow definitions are counted, and the count of values not drawn from a 4/8 px or modular scale is recorded.
stages.on_gate_failure: Extract from the rendered pages rather than the source; build-time values can be transformed before they reach the browser.

stages.name: Group into root causes
stages.goal: Reduce the symptom list to at most five causes, so remediation changes systems rather than pixels.
outputs: root-cause grouping with each symptom mapped to a cause
stages.exit_gate: Every symptom maps to a cause, and there are five or fewer causes. Ungrouped symptoms mean the analysis is incomplete.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-read the symptoms. Typical causes are a missing spacing/type/colour system, decoration substituting for hierarchy, no content model, and no motion rationale.

stages.name: Plan the remediation
stages.goal: Prioritise by blocking severity and recommend the smallest system change that removes the most symptoms.
stages.exit_gate: The plan is ordered CRITICAL to LOW, every S1 symptom appears in CRITICAL or HIGH, and the first items are system changes (define the three scales) rather than per-element restyling.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-order. Fixing twenty symptoms individually when one token file would fix eighteen is the most expensive possible path.

stages.name: Delete
stages.goal: Remove before adding — deletion resolves more slop than any quantity of new styling.
stages.exit_gate: Every decorative gradient, backdrop-blur layer beyond one, floating shape, glow shadow, unsubstantiated metric, filler adjective and unwired control identified in the plan is gone.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-check the plan; a symptom that survived deletion usually means its root cause is structural rather than decorative.

stages.name: Establish the three systems
stages.goal: Define spacing, type and colour as role-named tokens with contrast-checked pairs, and bind components to them.
stages.exit_gate: A modular type scale and a 4/8 px spacing scale are defined, colour is expressed as roles with every text/surface pair contrast-checked at WCAG AA, and lint fails on any raw value in a component.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix the palette or the surfaces until contrast passes. Do not weaken the accessibility target to preserve a colour.

stages.name: Rebuild hierarchy
stages.goal: Give each view exactly one primary element, distinguishable in at least three dimensions, and vary density deliberately between sections.
outputs: with the primary element identified per view and per breakpoint
stages.exit_gate: Each view has one primary element distinguishable in at least three of size, weight, colour, position, space, saturation or motion, and the squint/blur test identifies it at every breakpoint.
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove competing elements rather than strengthening the primary one. If two elements compete, the user chooses neither.

stages.name: Replace content
stages.goal: Put specific, true statements where filler was — this is the largest single contributor to "reads as generated".
stages.exit_gate: No unsubstantiated metric remains, no filler adjective remains, every claim is specific and true, and stock imagery has been replaced with the actual product, real data or nothing.
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate to the owner for real facts. Inventing a plausible metric to replace a fake one is worse than removing it.

stages.name: Add one deliberate detail
stages.goal: Restore character — remediation that only removes leaves a bland site, which is its own failure.
outputs: each documented with its purpose and risk
stages.exit_gate: At least one deliberate, non-generic design decision is present and documented, and no more than two differentiators compete.
stages.on_gate_failure: Choose one. Zero differentiators is blandness; five is incoherence.

stages.name: Motion rationalisation
stages.goal: Keep only motion that explains causality, continuity, feedback, hierarchy, state or relationship, with a complete reduced-motion path.
stages.exit_gate: Every surviving animation names a purpose; load-time entrance animation without a cause is removed; durations follow the hierarchy; prefers-reduced-motion yields a complete experience; nothing flashes more than three times per second.
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove the animation. Decorative motion is never worth defending.

stages.name: Verify no regression
stages.goal: Confirm the remediation did not break accessibility, responsiveness, performance or meaning.
outputs: contrast measurements at every breakpoint and theme
stages.exit_gate: Contrast passes AA everywhere, every interactive element is keyboard operable with a visible focus indicator, nothing overflows at 360 px, tap targets are at least 24x24 CSS px, and Core Web Vitals are within budget with no new layout shift.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix the regression before re-measuring slop. A less generic site that is unusable is not an improvement.

stages.name: Re-score and lock in
stages.goal: Measure the improvement and prevent decay.
stages.exit_gate: S1 count is zero, the slop score has fallen by at least 70%, visual-regression and token-lint gates run in CI, and a re-review date is scheduled.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 6 with the residual symptoms. If S1 symptoms remain, each needs a written justification accepted by the owner before ship.

quality_gates: A Design Direction Brief with explicit rejections exists before remediation begins.
Captures cover every template, state, breakpoint and theme.
100% of symptoms carry a catalogue ID and concrete evidence.
Symptoms grouped into five or fewer root causes.
Deletion precedes addition.
Spacing, type and colour-role tokens defined, contrast-checked at AA, and lint-enforced.
Zero raw visual values remain in component code.
Each view has exactly one primary element, distinguishable in at least three dimensions.
No unsubstantiated metric or filler adjective remains; every claim is specific and true.
At least one deliberate non-generic design decision documented; no more than two differentiators.
Every surviving animation names a purpose; reduced-motion path complete.
Accessibility, responsiveness and performance verified after remediation, not only before.
S1 count is zero and slop score reduced by at least 70%, or residuals are justified in writing.
CI gates prevent decay; re-review scheduled.
artifacts: capture set across states, breakpoints and themes
symptom table with IDs, evidence and severity
recomposed views with identified primary elements
post-remediation accessibility, responsive and performance verification
before/after slop score, verdict and CI gates

_headings: The three ideas that make this work
The failure this workflow must also avoid

workflows.name: analyze-existing-project
workflows.description: Understand an unfamiliar codebase or third-party repository from evidence — architecture map, conventions, health, license risk, security posture and fitness — before changing or adopting it.
workflows.trigger: Onboarding to an unfamiliar codebase before modifying it; evaluating a library, framework or MCP server for adoption; deciding whether to fork, wrap, contribute to or abandon a dependency; recording a repository into this knowledge base.
workflows.not_for: A repository already assessed recently and unchanged since (reuse the cached assessment); a security question, which needs workflows/security-review; a performance question, which needs workflows/performance-review; judging a project on style preference alone.
workflows.estimated_duration: 30-90 minutes for an adoption assessment; hours for a full codebase onboarding

stages.name: Establish purpose and constraints
stages.goal: Fix why the analysis is happening, because the required depth and the report shape both follow from it.
stages.exit_gate: The purpose is one of adopt, contribute, learn, onboard or record, and the integration mode is stated — dependency, vendored, MCP, fork or reference only.
stages.on_gate_failure: Ask the requester. An unscoped analysis produces a tour rather than an answer.

stages.name: Verify identity and status
stages.goal: Confirm this is the canonical upstream at the ref that will actually be used, and whether it is alive.
stages.exit_gate: The canonical upstream is confirmed, the ref under analysis matches what production pins, and archived or maintenance status is stated explicitly.
stages.on_gate_failure: Follow redirects and check release notes for renames. Analysing a fork and reporting the upstream's reputation is a common and damaging error.

stages.name: Read the machine-readable truth
stages.goal: Take facts from manifests, lockfiles, CI configuration and schemas rather than from prose.
outputs: exact dependency set with resolved versions
stages.exit_gate: The build, test and run commands are taken from manifests or CI rather than from the README, and every required environment variable and secret is enumerated.
stages.on_gate_failure: Run the commands. Documentation that cannot be executed is a hypothesis about the project, not a fact about it.

stages.name: Map the architecture
stages.goal: Produce a one-page map of entry point to core flow to outputs, with layering and extension points.
stages.exit_gate: A reader can trace one request or one command from entry to output using the map alone, and the public API boundary is identified.
stages.on_gate_failure: Follow one real execution path end to end with the debugger or with logging. A directory listing is not an architecture map.

stages.name: Assess health and maintenance
stages.goal: Determine whether this project will still be maintained when the dependency matters most.
outputs: WEAK or DEAD/UNSAFE — with the observable evidence and dates for each signal
stages.exit_gate: Every health signal cited is observable and dated, and the classification follows the rules in skills/repository-analysis rather than the star count.
stages.on_gate_failure: Record the health as UNKNOWN with the missing evidence named. An undated health snapshot is noise.

stages.name: Read the license
stages.goal: Establish what may legally be done with this code — the file, not the badge.
stages.exit_gate: The license file has been read; a null license is recorded as no-license-do-not-redistribute with vendoring prohibited; NOASSERTION or custom text is read for field-of-use and trademark restrictions; copyleft compatibility with the distribution model is stated.
stages.on_gate_failure: Prohibit vendoring and reference only. A high star count combined with no license file is the most common trap in this space.

stages.name: Assess quality and security posture
stages.goal: Determine whether the project's own engineering practices make it safe to depend on.
stages.exit_gate: What CI actually enforces is stated from the workflow files rather than from badges, known advisories at the resolved version are listed, and install-time behaviour is reviewed.
stages.on_gate_failure: Treat unenforced quality claims as absent. A badge is a claim; a workflow file is evidence.

stages.name: Run it
stages.goal: Execute the quickstart in a clean environment and measure the real onboarding friction.
stages.exit_gate: The quickstart has been executed on a clean environment at the version that would be adopted, and every divergence between documentation and observed behaviour is recorded.
stages.on_gate_failure: Record the failure as a finding. A quickstart that does not run is a maintenance signal with direct cost.

stages.name: Score fit and removal cost
stages.goal: Evaluate against this project's constraints rather than in the abstract, including the field everyone skips.
outputs: top three risks each with a detection method
stages.exit_gate: The fit table is weighted against the stated constraints, removal cost is quantified by call sites and files touched, and each of the top three risks has an observable detection method.
stages.on_gate_failure: Measure coupling by counting import sites. A dependency whose removal cost is unknown is a liability whatever its quality today.

stages.name: Report and record
stages.goal: Produce a verdict with conditions and file it where the next assessment can find it.
outputs: evidence table with URL or path and date per claim
stages.exit_gate: A verdict is stated with the conditions attached, every factual claim carries a URL or file path and a date, uncited statements are marked GENERATED, and the assessment is filed with a re-verification date.
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove or label the uncited claims. An assessment that cannot be traced cannot be trusted or reused.

quality_gates: Purpose and integration mode fixed before analysis begins.
Canonical upstream confirmed; the analysed ref matches what production pins.
Archived, disabled or maintenance status stated explicitly, never omitted.
Build, test and run commands taken from manifests or CI, not from prose.
A one-page architecture map traces one real path from entry to output.
Every health signal is observable and dated; stars alone are never a quality signal.
The license FILE was read; a null license yields no-license-do-not-redistribute and no vendoring.
CI enforcement read from workflow files, not from badges.
Advisories checked at the resolved version; install-time scripts reviewed.
The quickstart was actually executed in a clean environment at the target version.
Removal cost quantified; exit plan written.
Verdict stated with conditions; every claim cited or marked GENERATED; re-verification date set.
artifacts: quickstart execution record with friction log
weighted fit table with removal cost and exit plan
assessment report with verdict, conditions and evidence table
_headings: Failure modes specific to this workflow

workflows.name: architecture-review
workflows.description: Review an existing or proposed architecture against its stated requirements — boundaries, data ownership, consistency, failure behaviour, operability and reversibility — producing ADRs for what changes and a sequenced evolution plan.
workflows.trigger: A new design before implementation; an existing system that has outgrown its structure; a proposed service extraction, storage change or vendor adoption; a recurring incident class pointing at structure rather than code; or a one-way-door decision about to be taken.
workflows.not_for: Code-level review of a single change (use skills/code-review); a security-specific review (use workflows/security-review); a performance investigation (use workflows/performance-review); relitigating a decision that has an accepted ADR unless its stated revisit trigger has fired.
workflows.estimated_duration: half a day for a focused design review; days for a full system review

stages.name: Recover the requirements
stages.goal: Establish what the architecture is actually for, including the non-functional requirements that decide structure.
stages.exit_gate: Scale, latency, consistency, availability, durability, compliance, team size and budget are each stated with a number or an explicit "unknown", and unknowns that would change the design are flagged for resolution.
stages.on_gate_failure: Stop and gather them. Reviewing an architecture without its requirements produces an opinion about taste.

stages.name: Rank the quality attributes
stages.goal: Force the tradeoffs into the open, because unranked quality attributes produce a design that optimises nothing.
outputs: ranked quality attributes with numeric targets
and the pairs that conflict irreconcilably
stages.exit_gate: Attributes are ranked with numbers, and every conflicting pair is named — those conflicts are the escalation points for the owner rather than decisions for the reviewer.
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate the conflict. "Fast, consistent and cheap" is not a specification; one of the three must yield, and that is a business decision.

stages.name: Map the current or proposed structure
stages.goal: Draw what exists or what is proposed, at context and container level, with data flows and trust boundaries.
outputs: integration inventory with direction and contract per edge
stages.exit_gate: Every component, store, queue and external integration appears exactly once, every edge has a direction and a named contract, and every trust boundary is marked.
stages.on_gate_failure: Trace real requests through logs or traces to find the edges nobody documented. Undocumented integrations are where outages originate.

stages.name: Audit boundaries and data ownership
stages.goal: Check that each entity has one owner, each boundary has an interface, and the dependency direction is acyclic and deliberate.
stages.exit_gate: Every entity has exactly one owning component and every other access is a read through a contract; dependency cycles are either eliminated or recorded as accepted with a reason; the highest-coupling modules are identified by measured import counts.
stages.on_gate_failure: Name the owner. Two writers to one entity without a coordination mechanism is a data-corruption schedule, not a design.

stages.name: Audit consistency and failure behaviour
stages.goal: Verify that every integration has a designed answer to "what happens when this fails", and that consistency claims match the operations that need them.
outputs: degradation; consistency model per operation; invariant enforcement location
stages.exit_gate: No integration lacks a timeout, a bounded retry policy and a stated degradation; every invariant is enforced by a constraint rather than by convention; operations requiring strong consistency are identified and the rest are explicitly eventual.
stages.on_gate_failure: Design the missing failure behaviour before proceeding. An unspecified failure path is decided by whoever is on call, at 3 a.m., during the incident.

stages.name: Audit operability
stages.goal: Check whether the team that must run this can actually run it.
stages.exit_gate: Every component is deployable, observable and recoverable by the team that owns it; on-call load is within the team's capacity; and the cost model is stated rather than assumed.
stages.on_gate_failure: Simplify. A design the team cannot operate is a bad design regardless of its elegance — reduce components before adding headcount.

stages.name: Test against the alternatives
stages.goal: Establish whether the chosen structure is justified, including the simpler one nobody proposed.
outputs: comparison of the design against at least two alternatives
always including the simplest viable option and the do-nothing option
stages.exit_gate: At least two alternatives are compared against the ranked attributes, the simplest viable option is among them, and every additional component is justified by a requirement it serves.
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove the unjustified component. Complexity that cannot be traced to a requirement is decoration, and decoration in architecture is operational cost paid forever.

stages.name: Classify decision reversibility
stages.goal: Separate two-way doors from one-way doors, because they deserve opposite amounts of caution.
outputs: decision register with each decision classified as reversible or irreversible
the exit plan for irreversible ones
stages.exit_gate: Every proposed change is classified, every irreversible decision has a written exit plan or an explicit statement that none exists, and all irreversible decisions are on the escalation list for owner sign-off.
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate before proceeding. Taking a one-way door without sign-off is how teams end up unable to change anything.

stages.name: Write the ADRs
stages.goal: Record the decisions with the reasoning and the rejected alternatives, so the design survives the people who made it.
outputs: one ADR per consequential decision — context
stages.exit_gate: Every consequential decision has an ADR naming the alternatives that were rejected and why, and a reader of the ADRs alone could reconstruct the design and would not reverse it by accident.
stages.on_gate_failure: Write the missing ADR. A decision without a record will be reversed by the next person who finds it inconvenient.

stages.name: Sequence the evolution
stages.goal: Produce an order of work that retires risk early and keeps the system working at every step.
stages.exit_gate: The first milestone is a demonstrable end-to-end vertical slice rather than a layer, each milestone has an observable gate, the riskiest item is earliest, and every irreversible step is marked with the sign-off it requires.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-sequence. De-risking in the final milestone is not de-risking; it is discovering the risk when there is no time left to react.

quality_gates: Requirements recovered with numeric non-functional targets before any review of structure.
Quality attributes ranked; irreconcilable conflicts escalated rather than silently resolved.
Every component, store and integration appears once, with a direction and a named contract.
Every entity has exactly one owner; dependency cycles eliminated or accepted with a reason.
No integration lacks a timeout, bounded retry and stated degradation.
Invariants enforced by constraints, not by convention.
Every component deployable, observable and recoverable by its owning team.
On-call load within team capacity.
At least two alternatives compared, including the simplest viable option.
Every component traced to a requirement it serves.
Every decision classified reversible or irreversible, with exit plans for the latter.
An ADR exists per consequential decision, naming rejected alternatives.
First milestone is a walking skeleton; riskiest work is earliest; points of no return marked.
artifacts: ranked quality attributes with conflicts named
context, container and data-flow diagrams with trust boundaries
data ownership table and dependency graph
sequenced evolution plan with gates and points of no return

_headings: The three findings that matter most

workflows.name: bug-investigation
workflows.description: Systematic defect investigation from symptom to root cause — reproduce automatically, isolate to the smallest subsystem, test one hypothesis per change, fix the cause rather than the symptom, and file the lesson where the next agent will find it.
workflows.trigger: Any incorrect behaviour, crash, flake, regression, performance anomaly, security incident, or an agent about to make its third consecutive change to the same code without progress.
workflows.not_for: A known and understood defect with an agreed fix (implement it); a feature request described as a bug; cosmetic preference changes; a question about intended behaviour that documentation answers.
workflows.estimated_duration: 30 minutes for an isolated defect; hours for intermittent or cross-system failures

stages.name: Capture the symptom exactly
stages.goal: Record what is observed verbatim — the real error text, not a paraphrase — with the expected behaviour and how that expectation is known.
stages.exit_gate: The symptom is stated as observed text plus expected text, and the scope is bounded — which users, tenants, requests, data shapes, environments and versions are affected.
stages.on_gate_failure: Gather more observations before hypothesising. A paraphrased symptom sends the investigation in the wrong direction.

stages.name: Establish what changed
stages.goal: Correlate first-seen with deploys, dependency bumps, config changes, data migrations, feature flags, traffic shifts and schema changes.
outputs: candidate change list ranked by temporal and causal proximity
stages.exit_gate: Either a specific change is correlated with first-seen, or the investigation has established that nothing changed in the relevant window — which itself redirects the search to data or load.
stages.on_gate_failure: Widen the window and check upstream dependencies and third-party changes; a defect with no local cause often has a remote one.

stages.name: Reproduce automatically
stages.goal: Build the smallest deterministic reproduction, as a command or test, that fails reliably.
outputs: test or curl — plus its determinism rate and trigger variable
stages.exit_gate: A command exists that reproduces the failure, its determinism is measured (10/10, 3/10 or once), and the trigger variable is identified — input shape, timing, ordering, concurrency, state, environment, version or data volume.
stages.on_gate_failure: For intermittent failures, change the goal to raising the reproduction rate — parallelise, amplify timing, add load, replay recorded traffic — before hypothesising. Escalate if it cannot be reproduced at all.

stages.name: Observe the real error
stages.goal: Get the untruncated error at the correct layer, with symbols resolved and the exact input that caused it.
outputs: exact failing input with secrets redacted
version of every component in the path
stages.exit_gate: The error message has been read literally, the trace is resolved to source lines, and the failing input's shape is known — not merely its identity.
stages.on_gate_failure: Add instrumentation at the boundary of the suspected subsystem and reproduce again. Guessing from an unresolved trace wastes the rest of the investigation.

stages.name: Isolate
stages.goal: Reduce to the smallest subsystem in which the defect still reproduces.
outputs: the boundary inputs and outputs around it
evidence that everything outside is innocent
stages.exit_gate: A component has been identified such that the defect reproduces inside it and not when it is replaced by a known-good stub.
stages.on_gate_failure: Use bisection — git bisect on the regression range, binary search on the payload, halve the call path — and diff working against broken across environment, config, versions, data, flags, headers, timezone, locale and seed.

stages.name: Hypothesise and test
stages.goal: Test one falsifiable hypothesis per change, recording every attempt whether it confirms or kills.
stages.exit_gate: One hypothesis is confirmed by an observation that could have falsified it, and no attempt is repeated after being disproved.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 5 — a hypothesis that cannot be tested usually means the isolation is wrong. Never change two variables at once; if the bug disappears, nothing has been learned.

stages.name: Establish root cause
stages.goal: Ask down the causal chain to the level of the missing check, not just the immediate defect.
outputs: root cause at four levels — why it failed
stages.exit_gate: The chain reaches "why was it not caught", identifying the missing test, validation or review gate — which becomes a fix in its own right.
stages.on_gate_failure: Continue asking why. Stopping at level one yields a patch that returns in a different shape.

stages.name: Fix minimally
stages.goal: Apply the smallest change that removes the root cause, with no unrelated improvements bundled in.
outputs: plus the prevention fix for the missing gate identified in stage 7
stages.exit_gate: The fix addresses the cause rather than the symptom, contains no unrelated changes, and the missing gate from stage 7 has been closed — a test, a validation, a constraint or a lint rule.
stages.on_gate_failure: Split the change. A bug fix bundled with a refactor cannot be verified or reviewed, and a symptom patch must be replaced by a cause fix.

stages.name: Prove the fix
stages.goal: Verify with the automated reproduction, in the environment where the defect appeared, without collateral damage.
outputs: committed regression test named after the issue
stages.exit_gate: The reproduction passes, a regression test is committed with a name referencing the issue, the surrounding suite passes unchanged, and the fix is verified in the environment where the defect occurred — not only locally.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 6. Declaring success without a reproduction is a guess with a commit message.

stages.name: File the lesson
stages.goal: Put the knowledge where the next agent will find it before making the same mistake.
stages.exit_gate: The trap, its trigger and the safe alternative are recorded in a retrievable location, and any generalisable lesson has been filed with sources and a review date.
stages.on_gate_failure: File at minimum a gotcha entry. An unrecorded lesson will be paid for again.

quality_gates: An automated reproduction exists before any hypothesis is tested.
Determinism rate and trigger variable are recorded.
The full error was read literally at the correct layer, with symbols resolved.
The defect is isolated to a subsystem that reproduces it and only it.
One variable changed per test; the attempt log is complete, including killed hypotheses.
No disproved hypothesis is retried.
Root cause reaches "why was it not caught", and that gate is closed.
The fix is minimal, cause-directed and free of unrelated changes.
A regression test is committed and named after the issue.
The fix is verified in the environment where the defect appeared.
The lesson is filed in gotchas/, failure-modes/ or knowledge/.
artifacts: symptom statement with expected behaviour and scope
full resolved trace and exact failing input

_headings: The rule that makes this work
Failure modes specific to this workflow

workflows.name: build-website
workflows.description: End-to-end production of a website that looks designed rather than generated — research the direction, design the system, implement it, then pass the accessibility, slop and performance gates before anything is called finished.
workflows.trigger: A request to build, redesign or substantially extend a website, landing page, marketing site, dashboard or web application, where the visual result will be seen by users.
workflows.not_for: Backend-only work; a pure content edit; extending an existing surface inside an established design system (use the system, do not re-derive it); internal tooling where utility is the only requirement and the requester has said so.
workflows.estimated_duration: hours to days depending on scope; the gates are not optional at any scale

stages.name: Brief and content inventory
stages.goal: Establish the audience, the single most important action, the real content with its variance, and the constraints.
stages.exit_gate: Real content exists for every section, including shortest and longest plausible strings, and empty/one/many/error data states. Placeholder copy is not accepted.
stages.on_gate_failure: Request the content or write it and get sign-off. Designing against lorem ipsum produces layouts that break on first contact with truth.

stages.name: Visual design research
stages.goal: Build a written, defensible visual direction from real references instead of reaching for the default generated aesthetic.
stages.exit_gate: 15-30 references across four pools including anti-references, 5-8 fully decomposed with "why it works", and the brief states explicit rejections.
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate to the requester for references or for acceptance of a conventional direction, recorded as unresearched.

stages.name: Information architecture
stages.goal: Decide structure and priority before any pixels — what the user does here, what must be true to succeed, and in what order.
stages.exit_gate: Every view has exactly one primary element identified, and content that serves no task has been removed rather than placed.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-derive from the task list; a layout with no task behind it is decoration.

stages.name: Design system and tokens
stages.goal: Define the three systems that remove most slop before any component is drawn — spacing scale, type scale, colour roles.
stages.exit_gate: Every semantic colour token has a contrast-checked partner at WCAG AA, and every token is named by role rather than by appearance.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix the palette or the surfaces until contrast passes; never ship a token set that fails AA.

stages.name: Composition and craft
stages.goal: Design the views with deliberate hierarchy, asymmetry, density variation and craft details, plus one signature element specific to this product.
outputs: compositions for every view and state
stages.exit_gate: Each view's primary element is distinguishable in at least three dimensions, and the squint/blur test identifies it at every breakpoint.
stages.on_gate_failure: Reduce competing elements. If two elements compete, the user chooses neither.

stages.name: Motion design
stages.goal: Add animation only where it explains causality, continuity, feedback, hierarchy, state or relationship — with a complete reduced-motion path.
stages.exit_gate: Every animation names a purpose from the purpose test; nothing flashes more than three times per second; prefers-reduced-motion yields a complete, understandable experience.
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove the animation. Decorative motion is the strongest AI-slop signal and it is never worth defending.

stages.name: Implementation
stages.goal: Build the design in code with token-only styling, accessible primitives, every state implemented, and generated types at the data boundary.
stages.exit_gate: Zero raw colour, spacing or type values in component code, and every data-bound component implements empty, loading, error, partial and success states.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 4 or 5 — a hard-coded value usually means the token set is missing something the design needs.

stages.name: Accessibility gate
stages.goal: Prove a user with assistive technology can complete every critical task.
stages.exit_gate: All seven audit passes run at every breakpoint and theme; every critical task is completable by keyboard and by screen reader; no P1 barriers remain.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix and re-audit. An automated scan alone is not a pass — it detects roughly a third of issues.

stages.name: AI-slop gate
stages.goal: Detect and remove the signatures of generated design, with evidence per symptom and remediation aimed at root causes.
outputs: symptom table with IDs and evidence
stages.exit_gate: S1 symptom count is zero, or each remaining S1 has a written justification accepted by the requester, and at least one deliberate non-generic design decision is documented.
stages.on_gate_failure: Delete before adding — removal fixes more slop than any amount of new styling. Do not replace one cliché with another.

stages.name: Performance and SEO gate
stages.goal: Meet the agreed Core Web Vitals budget on the target device profile, and confirm the pages that should be found can be crawled, rendered and indexed.
outputs: baseline and after measurements by segment
stages.exit_gate: Core Web Vitals within budget at field p75 for the target profile, no regression in error rate or correctness, and every indexable page has its primary content in the served HTML or verified as rendered.
stages.on_gate_failure: Remove work before adding infrastructure — deletion, caching, code-splitting and image optimisation precede any scaling decision.

stages.name: Usability review
stages.goal: Walk every critical task cold, in success and failure states, on the audience's device profile.
outputs: barrier report with severity and smallest fix
stages.exit_gate: Every critical task is completable by a first-time user with no P1 barriers, in both success and failure states.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix the barrier with the smallest effective change; preferences are recorded separately and do not block.

stages.name: Browser verification and ship
stages.goal: Verify in real browsers at real breakpoints with real content, then release through a reversible, observable deploy.
stages.exit_gate: Critical journeys pass in the target browser matrix at every breakpoint with real content, both themes, reduced motion on and off, and the deploy has a verified instant rollback path.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix and re-verify; do not ship on a desktop-only pass or a retry that happened to go green.

quality_gates: Real content exists before design begins; no placeholder copy reaches stage 5.
A Design Direction Brief with explicit rejections exists before composition.
Spacing, type and colour-role tokens are defined and used exclusively by components.
Every semantic colour pair passes WCAG AA contrast, measured with a tool.
Every animation names a purpose and has a complete prefers-reduced-motion path.
Zero raw visual values in component code.
Every data-bound component implements empty, loading, error, partial and success states.
All seven accessibility passes run; every critical task keyboard and screen-reader operable.
AI-slop S1 count is zero, or each is justified in writing and accepted.
Core Web Vitals within budget at field p75 for the target device profile.
Every critical task walked cold in success and failure states with no P1 barrier.
Verified in the real browser matrix, at 360/768/1440 px, in both themes.
Indexable pages have their primary content in the served HTML or verified as rendered.
The deploy has a rehearsed instant rollback and observability wired from the first request.
artifacts: compositions for every view, state, breakpoint and theme
implementation with component and browser tests
slop symptom table, root causes, remediation and before/after score
browser verification matrix and deploy record

Failure modes specific to this workflow

workflows.name: deep-research
workflows.trigger: A question arrives whose answer will drive an engineering, architectural or adoption decision, where the cost of being confidently wrong exceeds the cost of researching it properly — technology selection, vendor or library evaluation, state-of-practice questions, regulatory or protocol questions, and any question where sources are known or likely to conflict.
workflows.description: Answer a research question with a graded, cited evidence set rather than an impression. Retrieval, verification, gap analysis and synthesis run as a loop that stops on a stated saturation condition, and every claim leaves the loop carrying its type, evidence level, confidence and the source that was actually reached.
not_for: A lookup with one authoritative answer and no conflicting sources — retrieve it and cite it; the loop is overhead.
A question nobody will act on. Research without a decision produces a document, not an answer.
A question about this codebase. Read the code; the repository is the primary source.
Anything requiring leaked, extracted or improperly obtained material. Refuse — see the exclusion policy.
A creative or generative task. There is no evidence set to converge on.
workflows.estimated_duration: 45-240 minutes, driven by the number of sub-questions and the depth of verification

stages.name: Scope the question
stages.exit_gate: The sub-question list exists, each sub-question names the source type that would settle it and what counts as sufficient evidence, and the decision, constraints and budget are all recorded.
stages.goal: Convert the question into 3-7 individually answerable sub-questions, each with the kind of source that would settle it and what would count as sufficient evidence. Record the decision the answer will inform, the constraints, and what is already established.
inputs: constraints: version, platform, budget, jurisdiction, deadline
what is already established, so it is not re-derived
outputs: a sub-question list with the evidence standard for each
a stated budget: maximum retrieval rounds or iterations
an explicit note of anything out of scope
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to the requester. A question that cannot be decomposed into checkable sub-questions is not yet a research question, and researching it will produce volume rather than an answer.

stages.name: Retrieve for primary sources
stages.exit_gate: Every sub-question has at least one source that was reached directly, and the source register records url, publisher, date, version and the reached-directly flag for each.
stages.goal: For each sub-question, reach the source that mints the fact — the specification, the official documentation for the exact version, the repository, the paper, the vendor's own page. Secondary sources are leads to primary ones, never substitutes. Record for every source: URL, publisher, date, the version it describes, and whether it was reached directly.
inputs: the sub-question list with its evidence standards
repository metadata for any repository under consideration
outputs: a source register: url, publisher, date, version, reached-directly flag
the raw findings per sub-question, attributed to a specific source
stages.on_gate_failure: If a sub-question has only secondary sources after the loop budget, mark it single-sourced or UNVERIFIED and continue. Do not promote a secondary source to primary by re-labelling it.

stages.name: Verify identity, date and standing
stages.exit_gate: Every source in the register has an identity confirmation and a verified_at date, its recency has been judged against the claim's shelf life, and anything unverifiable has been quarantined as UNVERIFIED rather than carried forward.
stages.goal: Confirm each source is what it appears to be — title, authors or publisher, identifier, version, date — then judge its date against the claim's shelf life rather than the source's prestige, and check its standing: authority, lifecycle status, license, self-interest.
inputs: the freshness windows per claim class
the scoring rules and their hard overrides
outputs: a per-source verification record with a verified_at date
lifecycle and license findings for any repository involved
a list of sources that could not be verified, quarantined rather than deleted
stages.on_gate_failure: Quarantine the unverifiable material as UNVERIFIED, exclude it from the active evidence set, and record what would make it gradeable. An unverifiable claim is not a weak claim; it is not a claim.

stages.name: Extract graded claims
stages.exit_gate: Every finding appears in the claim table as a single checkable claim with claim_type, evidence_level, confidence, and the specific source that supports that claim. Nothing rests on a trailing reference list.
stages.goal: Rewrite each finding as a single checkable claim and tag it: claim_type (fact, recommendation, experiment, opinion, hypothesis), evidence_level, confidence. Attach the specific source that supports THAT claim — a reference list at the end of a report supports nothing.
inputs: the claim taxonomy and evidence levels
outputs: a claim table: claim, type, evidence level, confidence, supporting sources, verified_at
a flag on every claim that rests on a single source
stages.on_gate_failure: A finding that cannot be written as a checkable claim is not a finding. Return it to the retrieve stage with the specific gap named, or drop it with a note.

stages.name: Seek independent corroboration
stages.exit_gate: Every load-bearing claim has either an independent second source with the independence judgement stated, or an explicit single-sourced flag with confidence capped at medium.
stages.goal: For every claim that will carry weight in the decision, find a second source with different provenance. Different provenance, not a different URL: three blogs restating one changelog are one source. Record where corroboration does not exist — single-sourced is a finding, not a defect to hide.
inputs: the claim table with its single-source flags
the decision, to determine which claims carry weight
outputs: corroboration status per load-bearing claim, with the independence judgement stated
an updated confidence for any claim that remains single-sourced
stages.on_gate_failure: Cap confidence at medium for any load-bearing claim that remains single-sourced, and say so in the report. Do not raise confidence because the claim is plausible or because it was repeated.

stages.name: Resolve conflicts by precedence
stages.exit_gate: Every disagreement between sources appears in the conflict register with the precedence rule applied, what was relied on, and what would settle it. No minority view has been dropped.
stages.goal: Where sources disagree, apply the precedence order — primary source reached directly, official documentation, peer-reviewed research, independent corroboration, reputable secondary analysis, community sources, and unsourced model output last, labelled GENERATED. Equal rank with genuine disagreement is a conflict: record both, state which was relied on and why, and say what would settle it.
inputs: the claim table and the source register
outputs: a conflict register: the sources, what each says, the rule applied, what was relied on, and what would settle it
a check that no minority view was silently dropped
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate the conflict as unresolved. An unresolved conflict reported honestly is a usable answer; one silently resolved in favour of the more convenient source is not.

stages.name: Self-critique the evidence set
stages.exit_gate: The critique record answers each of the five attack questions, and every gap that matters to the decision has either been closed by further retrieval or is listed as unresolved.
stages.goal: Attack the evidence set before synthesising: which claim would change the decision if it were wrong, and is it the best-verified one; where is the reliance on a single source; what was not looked for because it would have been inconvenient; which claim is really an inference dressed as a finding; what would a competent dissenter point to.
inputs: the claim table, conflict register and corroboration status
outputs: a critique record with the answers to each question
additional retrieval tasks for any gap that matters to the decision
stages.on_gate_failure: If the critique produces no gaps on a non-trivial question, it was not a critique. Re-run it against the specific decision rather than the general topic.

stages.name: Stop on saturation, not on exhaustion
stages.exit_gate: The stopping condition is recorded as either saturation (two rounds that changed nothing) or budget exhaustion, and what remains unresolved is listed.
stages.goal: Stop when two consecutive retrieval rounds add no claim that changes the answer or its confidence, or when the budget is reached. Record which condition stopped the loop, and what remains unresolved. An incomplete answer with a stated gap is usable; a complete answer with unstated gaps is not.
inputs: the retrieval log and the budget
outputs: the stopping condition that was met, with evidence for it
the list of what remains unresolved and why
stages.on_gate_failure: If neither condition is met and the budget is exhausted, stop anyway and report the budget as the reason. Running past budget produces volume, not confidence.

stages.name: Synthesise and report
stages.exit_gate: The report contains all seven parts including a non-empty UNKNOWN section, the answer addresses the stated decision, and a recommendation is given or its absence is justified by the evidence.
stages.goal: Produce the report: the answer with an overall confidence and its largest caveat; the answer against each stated constraint; the claim table; the conflict register; the UNKNOWN section; the method actually followed including dead ends and deviations; and the recommendation restated against the decision. State the answer first and restate it last — attention over a long document is unevenly distributed.
inputs: every artifact produced by the preceding stages
outputs: the research report in the seven-part structure
a recommendation, or an explicit statement that the evidence does not support one and what would
stages.on_gate_failure: If the report cannot state what would change the recommendation, the analysis has not identified its own load-bearing assumptions. Return to the critique stage.

quality_gates.gate: every claim has a source that was actually reached and that supports that specific claim
quality_gates.on_failure: the claim is downgraded to UNVERIFIED or removed; it is not left in with a citation that does not support it
restore the minority view to the conflict register with the precedence reasoning

quality_gates.gate: confidence matches the evidence level actually achieved
quality_gates.on_failure: downgrade the confidence; never upgrade the evidence level to match the confidence

quality_gates.gate: recency was judged against the claim's shelf life, not the source's prestige
quality_gates.on_failure: re-window the claim, re-verify it, or mark it stale

quality_gates.gate: the UNKNOWN section is present and non-empty, or explains why nothing is unknown
quality_gates.on_failure: the report is not deliverable; a report with no unknowns on a hard question did not look

quality_gates.gate: the answer addresses the stated decision, not a broader or more convenient question
quality_gates.on_failure: re-answer the question asked, or state explicitly why it cannot be answered as asked
remove it and record the exclusion; public reachability is not permission

artifacts: the research report, in the seven-part structure
the claim table with per-claim provenance
the source register with reached-directly and verified_at flags
the retrieval log, including dead ends
new knowledge articles or corrections for anything durable discovered

sources.note: Attention over long input is unevenly distributed — the reason the synthesise stage states the answer first and restates it last, and why the claim table exists as a compact structure rather than as prose.

workflows.name: knowledge-base-maintenance
workflows.description: Keep this repository trustworthy over time — validate, refresh sources, re-score, deduplicate, resolve conflicts, demote what no longer holds, regenerate every index, and record the run.
workflows.trigger: On a schedule (weekly validation, monthly source refresh, quarterly deep review); on new contribution; on a CI failure in any validation job; on an upstream event that invalidates content (release, rename, archive, license change, advisory, retraction); or on a user-reported correction.
workflows.not_for: Authoring new knowledge from scratch, which begins with workflows/research-before-coding; one-off typo fixes; content whose subject is private, leaked or prohibited — that is rejected, not maintained; deciding policy, which is a human decision recorded in an ADR.
workflows.estimated_duration: 15-30 minutes for a scheduled run; hours for a quarterly deep review

stages.name: Validate the current state
stages.goal: Establish a green baseline before changing anything, so new failures are attributable to this run.
stages.exit_gate: All validators report zero errors, or every pre-existing error is listed with its cause and a decision to fix it in this run.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix the validator failures before proceeding. Maintaining content on top of a red baseline produces changes nobody can attribute.

stages.name: Refresh repository-derived records
stages.goal: Re-fetch observable facts from the source of truth so repository metadata reflects today rather than the last run.
outputs: tier and trust_score; resolution log for renames and failures
stages.exit_gate: Every seed resolves to a canonical repository or is recorded as failed with a reason; renamed and archived repositories are detected; every star count carries its observation date; and null licenses are flagged no-license-do-not-redistribute.
stages.on_gate_failure: Quarantine the unresolvable seed rather than retaining a stale record. A repository record that cannot be resolved is a claim with no evidence.

stages.name: Verify external sources
stages.goal: Re-check the reachability and continued accuracy of cited non-repository sources.
stages.exit_gate: Every cited URL in active content was fetched; sources that fail consecutively are marked for review rather than silently retained; and papers remain verified against their primary source rather than a secondary aggregator.
stages.on_gate_failure: Downgrade the dependent claims and set claim_type or confidence accordingly. A dead source supporting a live fact is a defect.

stages.name: Scan for staleness
stages.goal: Find content past its review date or invalidated by an upstream event.
inputs: expires_at and verified_at across all frontmatter
stages.exit_gate: Every artifact past expires_at has an assigned action — re-verify, refresh, archive or quarantine — and fast-moving domains are on their 90-day cycle rather than a longer one.
stages.on_gate_failure: Quarantine the expired artifact out of the active index. Expired content retrieved with fresh-looking confidence is worse than absent content.

stages.name: Admit new submissions
stages.goal: Apply the admission standard to anything submitted since the last run.
stages.exit_gate: Every admitted artifact has resolvable sources actually fetched in this run, a claim_type supported by its evidence, a confidence the evidence justifies, an expires_at per the freshness policy, declared provenance, and a clean policy check.
stages.on_gate_failure: Quarantine rather than admit. An ungradeable artifact never enters the retrieval index, because a retrieved claim is acted upon with the confidence its label implies.

stages.name: Deduplicate and resolve conflicts
stages.goal: Prevent the same knowledge existing twice and the same question being answered two ways.
outputs: conflict entries in the prescribed format
stages.exit_gate: No two active artifacts make the same load-bearing claim with different content; every conflict is recorded with both sources, the likely cause, the side relied upon and what would settle it — never averaged and never silently resolved.
stages.on_gate_failure: Escalate load-bearing unresolvable conflicts. A hidden contradiction in a knowledge base is worse than a visible one.

stages.name: Re-score
stages.goal: Recompute quality scores from observable properties so tiers reflect current evidence rather than past judgement.
outputs: updated scores written back to frontmatter and metadata/scores.json
stages.exit_gate: Scores are computed by scripts/score/score_skills.py from the seven components rather than assigned by judgement, and every tier change is explained by an observable change in its inputs.
stages.on_gate_failure: Investigate the unexplained tier change. A score that moved without a cause indicates either a scoring defect or a content change that was not recorded.

stages.name: Demote and archive
stages.goal: Remove what no longer holds without losing the reason it was once believed.
outputs: deprecated or archived artifacts with successor links
stages.exit_gate: Every demotion records the reason and links a successor where one exists; nothing is deleted outright, because deleting a wrong decision loses the reasoning that prevents it recurring.
stages.on_gate_failure: Mark quarantined rather than deleting. An artifact that cannot be graded today may be gradeable with evidence that arrives later.

stages.name: Regenerate all derived artifacts
stages.goal: Rebuild every generated file from its records so no index can drift from its source.
outputs: regenerated indexes/ via extract_registries.py and build_index.py
stages.exit_gate: The generated-drift CI check is clean — regeneration produces byte-identical output to what is committed, proving no index was hand-edited.
stages.on_gate_failure: Revert the hand edit and fix the underlying record instead. A hand-edited generated index is silently wrong from the moment its source changes.

stages.name: Final validation and record
stages.goal: Confirm the repository is green after maintenance and record what changed.
outputs: re-scored and regenerated items with reasons
stages.exit_gate: All validators pass with zero errors, the changelog entry accounts for every change made in this run, and the run is committed with its date and trigger.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix before committing. Never commit maintenance that leaves the repository red.

quality_gates: Validation suite green before changes begin and after they end.
Every repository record resolved to a canonical upstream, with dated star counts.
Null licenses flagged no-license-do-not-redistribute; archived and renamed repositories detected.
100% of cited URLs in active content fetched during the run.
Papers verified against their primary source, never a secondary aggregator alone.
Every artifact past expires_at actioned; none left in the active index.
Admitted content has verified sources, supported claim_type, justified confidence and declared provenance.
No duplicate load-bearing claims; every conflict recorded in the prescribed format, never averaged.
Scores computed by script from observable properties, never assigned by judgement.
Demotions retain the file and record the reason with a successor link.
Generated artifacts byte-identical on regeneration; no hand-edited index.
CHANGELOG entry accounts for every change in the run.
No leaked, proprietary or prohibited material admitted at any stage.
artifacts: source verification results and failure history
regenerated indexes, cards and README statistics

workflows.name: performance-review
workflows.description: Establish whether a system meets its budget for its real users — baseline lab and field, profile end to end, rank by measured cost, fix in remove-first order, verify with the same method, and enforce the budget in CI so the gain does not decay.
workflows.trigger: Latency, throughput or page-load complaints backed by a symptom; a measured regression with a known approximate date; capacity planning for a known event; before scaling infrastructure; when setting budgets for a new product or redesign.
workflows.not_for: Optimising a path with negligible traffic; a correctness defect (use workflows/bug-investigation first — a fast wrong answer is worse); micro-optimisation where cost is dominated by a network call; a UX or design problem misreported as "slow".
workflows.estimated_duration: half a day for a focused regression; days for a full system review

stages.name: Agree the budget and the population
stages.goal: Fix the numbers and who they must hold for, because without them the work has no stopping condition.
outputs: numeric budget per metric — latency p50/p95/p99
throughput at an acceptable error rate
cost per 1k requests; target population segmented by device
stages.exit_gate: Every metric has a number and every number has a named population segment. A global target without segments hides the users actually complaining.
stages.on_gate_failure: Refuse to proceed. Optimising without a budget never finishes and proves nothing; escalate to the owner for the numbers.

stages.name: Capture the baseline
stages.goal: Measure the current state in both lab and field, with method, environment and date recorded.
outputs: lab baseline — reproducible controlled runs; field baseline — real-user percentiles by segment; recorded method
stages.exit_gate: Both baselines exist, percentiles are reported by segment rather than as means only, and the method is documented precisely enough that a second engineer could reproduce the numbers.
stages.on_gate_failure: Add instrumentation before continuing. Without a baseline there is no way to know whether any later change helped.

stages.name: Profile and attribute
stages.goal: Find where the time actually goes, before changing any code.
outputs: evidence; query counts per request; main-thread work; saturation points; network serial dependencies
stages.exit_gate: Every budget breach is attributed to a named component with a measured share of cost, and the top items account for the majority of the breach.
stages.on_gate_failure: Instrument deeper at the boundary of the suspected subsystem. Attributing by intuition leads to optimising the cold path.

stages.name: Rank and select
stages.goal: Decide what to fix, in what order, and explicitly what not to fix.
outputs: ordered remediation list by traffic share times per-request cost divided by effort
with the not-fixed items and their reasons
stages.exit_gate: The list is ordered by measured impact rather than by ease, the top item is addressed completely before the second begins, and every item below the noise floor is listed as not-fixed with a reason.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-rank against traffic data. Effort spent on a path nobody uses is the most common waste in performance work.

stages.name: Fix in remove-first order
stages.goal: Apply the cheapest, highest-yield class of fix before reaching for infrastructure.
outputs: changes applied in order — REMOVE work
stages.exit_gate: Each applied fix references the measured share of cost it addresses, and scaling infrastructure was not chosen while removal or reduction options remained unexhausted.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 3. A fix that does not correspond to a measured cost is a guess, and guesses compound.

stages.name: Verify with the same method
stages.goal: Prove the improvement on the same workload, in the same environment, at realistic peak.
stages.exit_gate: The same method and workload as the baseline were used, percentiles by segment are reported, the run covers at least 2x expected peak, and no other metric regressed.
stages.on_gate_failure: Revert or continue fixing. A latency improvement that raises error rate or cost is a regression, not a win.

stages.name: Confirm in the field
stages.goal: Check that the lab gain appears in real-user data, which is the only evidence about experience.
outputs: field deltas by segment over a defined observation window
with the segments that did not improve identified
stages.exit_gate: The affected segments show improvement in field data over the observation window, or the discrepancy between lab and field is explained — usually the lab measured something users do not do.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-profile against the field workload shape. A lab-only win is a measurement artefact until real users confirm it.

stages.name: Enforce the budget
stages.goal: Prevent the gain from decaying with the next ten feature merges.
outputs: CI budget gates that fail the build on regression
Lighthouse or k6 runs on affected routes
stages.exit_gate: Budget breaches fail CI rather than being noticed later, dashboards alert on p95 and p99 rather than on means, and a re-measurement date is scheduled.
stages.on_gate_failure: Add the gate manually for the affected paths. Performance without enforcement is a one-off event, and it decays at the rate of feature addition.

quality_gates: Numeric budget agreed per metric, with a named population segment, before any measurement.
Baseline captured in both lab and field, with method, environment and date recorded.
Percentiles reported by segment; no mean-only reporting.
Cost attributed by trace or profile before any code change.
Remediation ranked by measured impact, with not-fixed items and reasons listed.
Fixes applied in remove-first order; scaling chosen only after reduction is exhausted.
Verification uses the identical method and workload, at 2x or more of expected peak.
No regression in error rate, memory, cost or correctness.
Field data confirms the lab result for the affected segments.
Budgets enforced in CI; dashboards alert on p95/p99.
Re-measurement scheduled, because performance decays with feature additions.
artifacts: lab and field baselines with method, environment and date
ordered remediation list with not-fixed items and reasons
applied changes, each referencing its measured cost share
after-verification by segment with regression checks
field confirmation over the observation window
CI budget gates, dashboards, alerts and re-measurement date

Failure modes specific to this workflow

workflows.name: release-checklist
workflows.description: Take a change from merged to production and settled — version and changelog discipline, reproducible build, progressive rollout with health gates, instant rollback rehearsed, observation against leading indicators, and cleanup of flags and shims afterwards.
workflows.trigger: Any change reaching production or a published artifact; a scheduled release train; a hotfix under time pressure; a major version with breaking changes; or a release whose rollback path has never been exercised.
workflows.not_for: Local development iteration; a data migration, which needs workflows/../migration discipline on top of this one; a change with no consumer and no environment beyond a developer machine.
workflows.estimated_duration: 30 minutes for a routine patch; days for a major version with a migration guide

stages.name: Classify the change
stages.goal: Determine the version bump, the risk class and the rollout strategy the change actually requires.
inputs: commits and PRs since the last release
outputs: security; derived SemVer bump; risk class; chosen rollout strategy
stages.exit_gate: Every change is classified against the written public-surface definition, the version bump follows from the classification rather than from preference, and any breaking change forces a MAJOR bump without exception.
stages.on_gate_failure: Resolve the classification dispute before releasing. A SemVer lie destroys consumer trust more thoroughly than any bug.

stages.name: Prepare the release notes
stages.goal: Tell the consumer whether they need to act, and exactly what to do if they do.
outputs: with before-and-after code for every breaking change; migration guide for a MAJOR release
stages.exit_gate: Every entry answers "do I need to do anything?", every breaking change has a migration path with code, every deprecation names its removal version and date, and no entry reads "various fixes" or "improvements".
stages.on_gate_failure: Rewrite. A changelog that is a git log with headings forces every consumer to read the diff.

stages.name: Verify the gates
stages.goal: Confirm the artifact is correct before it is built for release, not after.
outputs: green gate results in order — lint
dependency and license scan; smoke test of the built artifact in a production-shaped environment; migration dry-run against a production-scale copy
stages.exit_gate: All gates pass in order with fail-fast behaviour, the built artifact has been smoke-tested rather than only the source, and migrations have been dry-run at production scale.
stages.on_gate_failure: Do not release. A hotfix under pressure still requires the gates that apply to its risk class; the reduced set is recorded, not assumed.

stages.name: Build reproducibly
stages.goal: Produce one artifact, immutable and promotable, that is identical to what was tested.
outputs: content-addressed artifact with an immutable tag or digest
stages.exit_gate: The artifact is built once and promoted unchanged through environments; dependencies and base images are pinned with integrity hashes; no secret appears in the image, the repository or the build log; and the same commit reproduces the same digest.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix the build. Rebuilding per environment means the tested artifact and the shipped artifact are different things.

stages.name: Confirm rollback before rollout
stages.goal: Know how to go back, how fast, and what cannot be undone — before there is a reason to need it.
outputs: documented rollback procedure with its measured duration
the list of irreversible effects with their forward-fix plans
stages.exit_gate: The previous version is retained and runnable, the kill switch has been exercised rather than assumed, and every irreversible effect — schema contraction, deleted data, sent messages, charged payments — has a forward-fix plan instead of a rollback plan.
stages.on_gate_failure: Do not roll out. A rollback path never tested is a hypothesis, and it is tested during the incident if not before.

stages.name: Deploy configuration first
stages.goal: Land the backwards-compatible prerequisites so the code deploy is not also a configuration deploy.
inputs: feature flags in their off state
outputs: schema expanded compatibly with the previous application version
stages.exit_gate: Every required configuration value is present and validated at boot with an actionable failure message; flags exist in their off state; and the schema remains compatible with the currently running version.
stages.on_gate_failure: Fix configuration before deploying code. An app that boots with missing configuration and fails later produces a business bug instead of a deploy failure.

stages.name: Roll out progressively
stages.goal: Expose the change to a small, comparable cohort first and expand only on evidence.
outputs: rollout steps with dwell time per step
health-gate results at each step — readiness green
stages.exit_gate: Each step passes its health gate before the next begins, mixed-version compatibility holds throughout, and the rollout can be halted at any step by flipping the kill switch.
stages.on_gate_failure: Halt and roll back. A canary nobody compares is a slow rolling update, and a breached gate is a decision already made.

stages.name: Observe against leading indicators
stages.goal: Detect a problem from telemetry before users report it.
outputs: observation record over the dwell window — error rate
and the specific metrics this change could affect; deploy marker attribution confirmed
stages.exit_gate: The observation window has elapsed with metrics flat or improved, deploy markers make attribution possible, and alerts fired on nothing that required action.
stages.on_gate_failure: Roll back first, diagnose second. Restoring service precedes understanding; the artifact and telemetry remain for analysis afterwards.

stages.name: Publish and announce
stages.goal: Make the release discoverable and upgradeable by its consumers.
outputs: registry publication verified by a clean-environment install
updated support window and EOL dates
stages.exit_gate: The published artifact has been installed and exercised from a clean environment, the tag is immutable, the documentation states which version it describes, and the support window is published with dates.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-publish. Assuming the upload succeeded because CI was green is how consumers discover the release first.

stages.name: Settle and clean up
stages.goal: Close the release rather than leaving it half-finished, and learn from it.
outputs: fully-released flags scheduled for removal with dates
temporary shims and compatibility layers dated for deletion
retrospective with the estimate-versus-actual delta and any surprise
stages.exit_gate: Every flag and shim has a removal date rather than an indefinite lifetime, the release record is complete, and any surprise is captured as a gotcha, a failure mode or a gate improvement.
stages.on_gate_failure: File the removal dates at minimum. Flag debt is real debt, and forty live flags nobody understands is a future incident.

quality_gates: Every change classified against the written public-surface definition; breaking changes force MAJOR.
Changelog answers "do I need to act?" per entry; every breaking change has migration code.
All gates pass in order; the built artifact is smoke-tested, not only the source.
Migrations dry-run against a production-scale copy; schema stays compatible with the running version.
Artifact built once, reproducibly, content-addressed, promoted unchanged; no secrets in image or logs.
Rollback rehearsed and timed before rollout; irreversible effects have forward-fix plans.
Configuration validated at boot and deployed before the code that uses it.
Progressive rollout with health gates at every step; mixed-version compatibility verified.
Kill switch exercised, not assumed.
Observation window elapsed with metrics flat or improved; deploy markers enable attribution.
Published artifact verified by a clean-environment install; documentation versioned.
Flags and shims carry removal dates; release record and retrospective filed.
artifacts: change classification and derived version bump
gate results and artifact smoke test
content-addressed artifact with SBOM and signature
rollback procedure with measured duration and rehearsal record
rollout record with per-step health gates
published tag, verified install and versioned documentation
flag and shim removal schedule, release record and retrospective
