workflows.name: research-before-coding
workflows.description: The mandatory gate before any non-trivial implementation: understand the request, research the unknowns, compare options, verify the evidence, and produce a Research Decision Record that implementation must follow.
workflows.trigger: Any task that will produce code intended to be kept, especially one naming a specific library, framework, API, cloud service or protocol, or one containing an implicit technology choice ("build me auth", "add caching", "make it fast").
workflows.not_for: One-line typo fixes; purely local refactoring proved correct by an existing suite; explicitly disposable spikes; tasks whose conventions are already pinned in the repository's own AGENTS.md (read that instead of the internet); work where a human has already fixed the library, version and pattern.
workflows.estimated_duration: 20-90 minutes depending on risk class and unknown count

stages.name: Understand and frame
stages.goal: Restate the task, name every implicit technology decision it assumes, classify the risk, and define the observable success test.
stages.exit_gate: At least one implicit choice is named, or the task is explicitly marked research_skipped with a written reason.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to the requester for clarification; do not proceed on an unframed task.

stages.name: Load local context first
stages.goal: Answer as much as possible from the cheapest and most specific sources before searching the internet.
stages.exit_gate: Every unknown is either answered from local context or carried forward with a statement of what external evidence would resolve it.
stages.on_gate_failure: Record the unknown as UNRESOLVED and continue; never invent an answer to close the gap.

stages.name: Research the unknowns
stages.goal: Gather evidence per unknown from official documentation for the correct version, the official repository, and at least one independent source.
inputs: required confidence from the risk class
stages.exit_gate: At least two independent provenances per load-bearing unknown, or the unknown is marked UNRESOLVED with the resolving evidence named.
stages.on_gate_failure: Downgrade the claim's confidence and record the single-sourcing explicitly; escalate if the decision is high-risk.

stages.name: Compare options
stages.goal: Build a decision matrix over real candidates, always including a hand-roll or do-nothing row, and reject at least one option for a stated reason.
stages.exit_gate: At least two options compared, weights fixed before scoring, and every rejected option has a specific, checkable reason.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 3 for the missing candidate; a matrix with one row is not a comparison.

stages.name: Verify the chosen option
stages.goal: Apply the twelve evidence-validation checks to the selected dependency or approach, including existence, status, license, version-specific API and maintenance outlook.
stages.exit_gate: Every load-bearing claim has confidence at or above the level the risk class requires, and each carries a verified_at date.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-verify, choose the runner-up, or escalate. Never proceed on an unverified load-bearing claim.

stages.name: Write the Research Decision Record
stages.goal: Produce the artifact that implementation must follow, including the decision, the why, the rejections, the evidence, the open risks and the validation plan.
stages.exit_gate: A reader who was not present could execute the plan without asking questions, and every load-bearing claim in it is cited with a date.
stages.on_gate_failure: Rewrite until the record is self-sufficient; do not start implementation with an incomplete record.

stages.name: Plan the implementation
stages.goal: Sequence the work into steps, each with an observable completion condition, ordered riskiest-first, with a walking skeleton as the first milestone.
stages.exit_gate: Every step has a checkable done-condition, dependencies are explicit, and stop conditions and escalation triggers are written down.
stages.on_gate_failure: Re-decompose; a step without a gate is a hope, not a plan.

stages.name: Implement against the record
stages.goal: Build to the plan. When reality contradicts the research, stop and update the record rather than improvising silently.
stages.exit_gate: The implemented solution matches the record, or the record was updated before the divergence took effect.
stages.on_gate_failure: Halt and re-enter stage 5 with the contradicting observation; silent improvisation converts verified research back into hallucination.

stages.name: Validate
stages.goal: Run the validation plan defined in stage 6 and add regression tests for each open risk.
stages.exit_gate: Every item in the validation plan passes, and each open risk has a regression test or a recorded acceptance.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 8 with the failing evidence; do not weaken an assertion to pass.

stages.name: Feed back into the knowledge base
stages.goal: Convert the experience into durable memory so the next agent does not relearn it.
stages.exit_gate: What worked, what failed, what was outdated and what was missing are each recorded somewhere retrievable, or explicitly judged not durable.
stages.on_gate_failure: File the minimum — a gotcha entry for the trap and a verified_at refresh for the sources used.

quality_gates: No implementation code exists before the Research Decision Record does.
Every load-bearing claim in the record carries a URL, a page date and a confidence level.
At least one option was rejected for a stated, checkable reason.
100% of cited URLs were actually fetched during the run.
Chosen dependencies verified to exist, with license known, status known and version pinned.
Any repository with license null is flagged no-license-do-not-redistribute and never vendored.
Security-critical primitives were escalated or adopted, never hand-rolled.
The record's outcome was fed back into the knowledge base.

workflows.name: security-review
workflows.description: Threat-model, audit and remediate — covering application code, data flows, supply chain, CI/CD and the agent/tool/MCP surface that conventional checklists miss, with every finding backed by a concrete exploit path.
workflows.trigger: Before any release touching auth, sessions, payments, PII, file upload or admin surfaces; when adding an agent, tool integration, MCP server or any code-execution path; when adding a dependency that runs at install time; after a security incident; and periodically on production systems.
workflows.not_for: Code with no attack surface (a local script with no external inputs) — record that and skip; as a substitute for an authorised penetration test where one is contractually required; as a way to generate a long list of theoretical findings, which produces alert fatigue and hides the real issue.
workflows.estimated_duration: half a day for a focused change review; days for a full system audit

stages.name: Scope and classify
stages.goal: Establish what is in scope, what data is involved, and who benefits from breaking it.
stages.exit_gate: Every entry point is enumerated — HTTP routes, webhooks, queues, uploads, CLI, agent tools, MCP servers, CI, admin UI — and every data class is mapped to where it is stored, processed and logged.
stages.on_gate_failure: Widen the enumeration. A missed entry point is a missed finding, and the miss is invisible in the report.

stages.name: Threat model
stages.goal: Diagram data flows, mark trust boundaries, apply STRIDE per boundary and rank the resulting threats.
outputs: ranked threat list with expected controls
stages.exit_gate: Every trust boundary has a STRIDE pass, and every retained threat names the control expected to mitigate it — the audit then checks whether that control exists, is correct, and cannot be bypassed.
stages.on_gate_failure: Return to stage 1; an incomplete boundary map produces an incomplete threat list.

stages.name: Read the code
stages.goal: Audit injection and input handling, authn and sessions, authz at object and function level, secrets and configuration, data protection, and availability and abuse.
outputs: conditions and evidence per checklist area
stages.exit_gate: Every checklist area has been grepped across the whole codebase rather than sampled, and each item either cites a location or records "not present".
stages.on_gate_failure: Complete the sweep. A sampled audit reports the defects it happened to look at.

stages.name: Supply chain
stages.goal: Review dependencies, build and CI/CD for the risks that live outside the application code.
outputs: advisory triage at resolved versions with reachability
stages.exit_gate: Advisories are triaged at the RESOLVED version with a reachability judgement, install-time scripts are reviewed or disabled, CI credentials are least-privilege and short-lived, and no workflow grants production access to pull-request code.
stages.on_gate_failure: Block the release for unresolved critical advisories with a reachable path; record accepted risks with owner, expiry and compensating control.

stages.name: Agent, tool and MCP surface
stages.goal: Audit the attack surface that conventional checklists miss, whenever agents or tool integrations exist.
stages.exit_gate: Every tool has an assigned capability tier at or below what its use requires; filesystem tools are rooted; egress is allowlisted with cloud metadata endpoints blocked; tier-2-or-above actions require confirmation when triggered by untrusted content; and every side-effecting call is attributable in a log.
stages.on_gate_failure: Disable the over-scoped tool. Capability creep is not mitigated by documentation.

stages.name: Injection and abuse testing
stages.goal: Attempt the attacks the threat model predicts, in an authorised environment only.
outputs: with reproduction steps for anything that succeeded
stages.exit_gate: Every high-ranked threat has been exercised in an environment the reviewer is authorised to test, and results are recorded whether they confirm or refute the control.
stages.on_gate_failure: Do not test. Escalate for authorisation, or convert the item into a code-reading finding with its limitation stated. Testing a third-party system without authorisation is prohibited by this workflow.

stages.name: Grade and report
stages.goal: Rank findings by exploitability times blast radius, each with a standard reference, a remediation and a verification test.
stages.exit_gate: Every finding above INFO has a concrete exploit path, severity is derived from exploitability times blast radius rather than from category prestige, and every finding names the test that proves its remediation.
stages.on_gate_failure: Downgrade findings without an exploit path to INFO and state why. Eighty theoretical findings hide the one that matters.

stages.name: Remediate
stages.goal: Fix in severity order, using trusted implementations rather than hand-rolled primitives.
outputs: one per finding or per coherent group
stages.exit_gate: All CRITICAL findings are fixed before release; HIGH findings are fixed or carry an accepted-risk entry with owner, expiry and compensating control; no security primitive is hand-rolled.
stages.on_gate_failure: Block the release for unfixed CRITICAL findings, or escalate for a written risk acceptance. Never hand-roll crypto, token signing, password storage or payment flows — adopt or escalate.

stages.name: Verify remediation
stages.goal: Run each finding's verification test and confirm the failure mode is now impossible rather than merely unlikely.
stages.exit_gate: Every remediated finding's verification test passes, regression tests are committed, and a re-scan of the affected area produces no new findings.
stages.on_gate_failure: Reopen the finding. A claimed fix that was not verified is not a fix.

stages.name: Harden and record
stages.goal: Close the systemic gaps the findings revealed and make the audit repeatable.
outputs: lint rules for the defect classes found
stages.exit_gate: Each defect class that produced a finding has a preventive gate in CI or in lint, the threat model reflects the current system, accepted risks are registered with expiry dates, and the next audit is scheduled.
stages.on_gate_failure: File at minimum the accepted-risk register and the next-audit date; a finding fixed without a gate will recur.

quality_gates: Threat model drawn with trust boundaries before any code was read.
STRIDE applied per boundary; every retained threat names its expected control.
All entry points enumerated, including agent tools, MCP servers and CI.
Code swept across all seven checklist areas, whole-codebase rather than sampled.
Advisories triaged at resolved versions with a reachability judgement.
Install-time scripts reviewed; CI credentials least-privilege; no PR code with production access.
Agent/tool/MCP surface audited whenever it exists, with capability tiers assigned.
No unauthorised testing of any third-party system, at any stage.
100% of findings above INFO carry a concrete exploit path.
Severity from exploitability times blast radius, never from category prestige.
Every finding has a remediation and a verification test; remediations are verified.
No security primitive hand-rolled anywhere in the remediation.
Secret scanning covers git history, not only the working tree.
Accepted risks recorded with owner, expiry and compensating control.
No leaked system prompts, private model internals or proprietary weights used, vendored or reproduced.
artifacts: threat model with STRIDE enumeration and ranked threats
agent/tool/MCP capability and injection test report
graded findings report with remediations and verification tests
CI security gates and lint rules added
